newsitem.title: USA: ITT Educational considers adding curricula.
newsitem.headline: ITT Educational considers adding curricula.

text.p: ITT Educational Services Inc said Wednesday it is considering several growth options, including expanding its college base and adding curricula at the associate's and bachelor's degree levels.

"We are uniquely positioned to serve a wide range of specialty technology niches," Rene Champagne, chairman, said in a statement. "For example, the recently introduced chemical technology and computer visualization technology bachelor degrees were developed in collaboration with our corporate customers -- future employers of our graduates."
He added he is optimistic about maintaining long-term growth for net earnings this year and next, based on new student enrollment. ITT operates 59 technical institutes in 26 states.

ITT said the number of first-time students enrolling in the September 1996 term rose 16 percent to 7,271 from 6,290 a year ago. As of September 30, total student enrollment reached an historic high of 23,971 students, compared with 21,863 students for the 1995 period.
Earlier, ITT reported third quarter earnings of $0.37 a share, up from $0.30 a year ago. For the nine-month period, earnings were $0.65 a share, up from $0.51 last year.
